chunks: Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The traveler's prayer is at the time the sun declines, because there is no prayer before it during travel. And if he wishes, he may delay it until the time of Dhuhr in residency, except that it is better for him to pray it at the beginning of its time, when the sun declines.
ai.seo_question: When should a traveler perform their prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of Zurara, establishes the preferred timing for the traveler's Dhuhr prayer at the moment of solar zenith (Zawal), distinguishing it from the resident's practice of delaying it. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for performing prayers at the beginning of their designated time (Iqdam) unless there is a valid reason to delay, thereby emphasizing the spiritual discipline of the traveler. This ruling reflects the broader principle of facilitating worship while maintaining the integrity of prayer times during journeys.
